It seems like everyone has a Substack these days: Keir Starmer, Charli XCX, Pamela Anderson and, as Lightbulb readers know, Nigel Farage. We covered his first essay on the platform, which argued British society discriminates against white people, in a recent edition. Today, Terri White takes Farage to task on another of his assertions: that white working-class boys are the main demographic being overlooked in education.White doesn’t doubt that they face many challenges, but a new report shows that it’s “actually girls suffocating inside the bell-jar of an escalating crisis.” White working-class girls still do a little better at GCSE-level than boys, but the gap is closing.  And these same girls now have worse absence rates, report enjoying school the least, and go on to earn lower wages even when they’ve left school with higher qualifications, White writes.When he’s not writing his Substack, Farage can be found fist-fighting Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey on the BBC’s Question Time. Except, of course, he has never done that—despite what you might have seen online. On today’s episode of Media Confidential, Alan Rusbridger and Lionel Barber discuss how a deepfake video of Reform’s leader doing exactly this has spread on social media.Alan and Lionel also discuss Lachlan Murdoch’s latest acquisition at Fox: streaming service Roku. It’s the Murdoch family’s biggest ever deal. Perhaps Rupert’s actual “eldest boy” is a more “serious” person than the fictional sons of media mogul Logan Roy in Succession.Speaking of things you can stream on Murdoch’s new TV box, a bumper edition of our Culture newsletter hit our subscribers’ inboxes this morning, containing a double dose of sci-fi. First up, Alexander Larman reviews Steven Spielberg’s latest film Disclosure Day. Then David Barnett considers why the BBC has put Doctor Who on ice (they’re too busy mopping Andrew Bailey’s blood off the floor—JOKING we know the fight was fake.)Reform UK’s fight with Labour in the Makerfield byelection is very real, however, with voters heading to the polls in the Greater Manchester electorate today to choose their next representative. And they might just be choosing the nation’s next prime minister too. As Andrew Adonis recently wrote, “for once, the hype is valid. The Makerfield byelection really matters.” Good luck today Mancunians and we’ll see you on the other side.As always, email your thoughts to ben.clark@prospectmagazine.co.uk.

Benjamin ClarkHead of digital audience
